in_text_mentions: ly seen in 894 (89.4%) neonates, among which 428 (47.87%) were females and 466 (52.12%) were males. The most common site of location was nose. Epstein pearls were seen in 891 (89.1%) newborns with 399 (44.78%) females and 492 (55.21%) males. The most common site of location was midline of palate; it was seen over gingiva (Figure 6) in 10 (1.12%) newborns. Mongolian spots (Figure 9) were seen in 847 (84.7%) newborns: 380 (44.86%) females and 467 (55.13%) males; most common site of location was lumbosacral area. It was multiple in 47 (5.54%) newborns. Milia (Figure 4) was seen in 18.3% newborns.
